content.summary_of_the_paper: The manuscript improves inference speed in scene understanding by detecting temporal change in semantics with a separate dense prediction model. Pixels with constant semantics are inferred by copy-pasting predictions from the previous frame. Pixels with changed semantics are inferred by a pruned model. The extent of pruning is controlled in stochastic manner by conditioning on features from the previous frame. When the extent of temporal dynamics exceeds a threshold, the current frame is inferred through the standard non-pruned model. Experiments on Cityscapes reveal inference speedups from 28% to 48%.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1. Improving the inference speed of scene understanding methods is an important goal towards autonomous robotics systems
2. A separate network for change detection may be useful in various other applications. 

Weaknesses
1. Current predictions in distorted pixels do not seem to take advantage of features from the previous frame (these features are only used for selecting the pruned layers). However, research in dense semantic forecasting shows that this should be beneficial for performance [a,b].
2. Pixels corresponding to large scene dynamics get the least capacity (they get recognized with a pruned model). This does not feel right from the mission-safety viewpoint.
3. Many implementation details are missing such as the structure and latency of feature extractor or ways to deal with lateral connections from the encoder to the decoder. It would be helpful to ablate Ldice.

Missing related work
[a] Real-Time Segmentation Networks Should be Latency Aware. ACCV 2020.
[b] Dense Semantic Forecasting in Video by Joint Regression of Features and Feature Motion. TNNLS 2021.
[c] RTFormer: Efficient Design for Real-Time Semantic Segmentation with Transformer. NeurIPS 2022.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel framework to speed up any architecture for real-time video segmentation tasks. This paper performs partial network evaluation and reusing temporally consistent features across video frames. In addition, inter-frame distortion is used to capture spatial-temporal information across frames.  The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on three datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1)This paper introduces the dynamic block pruning mechanism based on spatial-temporal locality.
2)This paper uses the mask generator for feature transformation and reuse based on the distortion between adjacent frames.
3)The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art on Cityscapes datasets, and some ablation studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of each component.
4)The paper is generally well-written.  

Weaknesses:
1) My main concern is the main novelty. In this paper, spatial-temporal reuse is used based on the distortion between adjacent frames. This method is more common in considering the difference between different frame features.
2) I'm not sure if this article overclaims this “the proposed framework can speed up any architecture with skip-connections for real-time vision tasks”. 
The authors only conduct their method on DDRNet-39 and DDRNet-23-Slim to demonstrate its superiority of speed. I consider that authors should do more experiments to verify its versatility on other architecture with skip-connections.
3) This article uses this “input-dependent block pruning” module. In the segmentation field, many methods are based on conditional random fields. Can you elaborate on the advantages?
4) I also consider that the effectiveness of this method is not advanced. In table 8, authors compare their method STMG-DDR39 with other real-time segmentation methods on CamVid while MSFNet, a method proposed in 2019, attained similar mIoU and much fast speed (STMG-DDR39: 75.5 mIoU, 70.2 FPS; MSFNet: 75.4 mIoU, 91.0 FPS).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The clarity is good. The quality of the whole paper is satisfying. However, the novelty of the whole paper is limited.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper proposes a speed up strategy for video segmentation. The pruning technique and K-D loss have been widely used for segmentation task[1]. Also, in the experimental section,  the speed advantage is negligible especially compared to the performance degradation.  Overall, I suggest a borderline reject for the current version.
[1] Structured Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposed an efficient framework for real-time video semantic segmentation that exploits the spatial-temporal locality of videos. The framework reuses the features from previous frames, and perform partial evaluation of the backbone network by taking into account the differences between two consecutive frames. This partial network evaluation is done using an input-dependent
gating mechanism that decides which features and blocks to prune. The framework is model-agnostic
and can be applied to any semantic segmentation models with residual backbone networks to speed
up their inference. The authors validated our method on two benchmark datasets with different semantic
segmentation models and showed that it significantly improves inference-time speed at the expense of
marginal drop in accuracy compared to baselines approaches that achieve lower inference speed-ups
with similar decreases in model accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The paper is well-written and easy to understand.
2. A framework to speed up the inference of residual backbone networks for real-time video semantic segmentation by performing partial network evaluation and reusing temporally consistent features across frames is proposed.
3. A method to capture spatial-temporal information across frames based on inter-frame distortion without heavy optical flow computations is proposed.
4. The proposed method is validated on two benchmarks against multiple state-of-the-art real-time video segmentation models.


Weakness:
1. The speed improvement  over DDR23-slim baseline (while dropping accuracy by ~1.4%) is small as shown in table 1.
2. For tha ablation study, i don't see the proposed method's results are convincing. The performance improvemnt is not obvious.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper's experimental results are not convincing. so i think it can be accepted.

content.title: Distortion-Aware Network Pruning and Feature Reuse for Real-time Video Segmentation
content.abstract: Real-time video segmentation is a crucial task for many real-world applications such as autonomous driving and robot control. Since state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models are often too heavy for real-time applications despite their impressive performance, researchers have proposed lightweight architectures with speed-accuracy trade-offs, achieving real-time speed at the expense of reduced accuracy. In this paper, we propose a novel framework to speed up any architecture with skip-connections for real-time vision tasks by exploiting the temporal locality in videos. Specifically, at the arrival of each frame, we transform the features from the previous frame to reuse them at specific spatial bins. We then perform partial computation of the backbone network on the regions of the current frame that captures temporal differences between the current and previous frame. This is done by dynamically dropping out residual blocks using a gating mechanism which decides which blocks to drop based on inter-frame distortion. We validate our Spatial-Temporal Mask Generator (STMG) on video semantic segmentation benchmarks with multiple backbone networks, and show that our method largely speeds up inference with minimal loss of accuracy.
